subject.title: Support GCP broker auth via metadata server / Workload Identity

question: Should Crabbox add metadata-server or Workload Identity token acquisition as a supported brokered GCP credential source for Node coordinators, and keep other runtimes key-only unless they prove metadata support?
rationale: This changes provider authentication and readiness semantics, so automation should not choose the permanent credential boundary without maintainer intent.

options.title: Provider-local metadata fallback
options.body: Support static key-pair auth when both variables are set, metadata-server tokens only when no key variables are set and the metadata endpoint is reachable, and explicit failure for partial key configuration.

options.title: Keep static key-only broker auth
options.body: Reject the keyless coordinator path for now and leave GCP brokered auth documented as service-account-key based.

options.title: Defer for broader runtime design
options.body: Hold this issue until coordinator runtime detection and provider-auth abstractions are designed across cloud-hosted Node deployments.

recommendation.title: Provider-local metadata fallback
recommendation.body: Support static key-pair auth when both variables are set, metadata-server tokens only when no key variables are set and the metadata endpoint is reachable, and explicit failure for partial key configuration.

likelyOwner.reason: The GCP broker implementation and recent GCP hardening history point to this person as the best available owner for the provider-auth boundary choice.
